security_audit.summary: The reviewed files are mostly Markdown guidance and code samples, and most static hits are false positives from formatting, Python imports, or loopback debug addresses. Confirmed risks remain around .env handling, generated debug shell tasks, runtime package installation, and an unpinned npx MCP sample. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Do not always overwrite .env. Preserve existing values, ask for confirmation, and document that load_dotenv(override=True) can shadow deployment variables.
Pin @playwright/mcp to a reviewed version or require user confirmation before generating npx -y @latest commands.
Generate VS Code shell tasks only after the user confirms the entrypoint and ports. Keep debugpy bound to localhost.
Ask before running generated apps or installing dependencies. Separate code generation from execution in default workflows.

content.value_statement: Agent teams need a reliable way to scaffold Microsoft Agent Framework projects. This skill guides Python agents, workflows, HTTP server mode, and debugging setup.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of Python Agent Framework agents and multi-agent workflows.
Shows HTTP server wrapping with Azure AI Agent Server packages.
Provides VS Code debug task and launch configuration templates.
Includes Foundry model selection and environment configuration guidance.
Includes sample patterns for MCP tools, threads, streaming, and workflow edges.
Recommends pinned SDK package versions for compatibility.
limitations: It does not deploy agents to Azure or evaluate existing agents.
It assumes Python and Microsoft Agent Framework beta package versions.
Generated projects still require valid Azure AI Foundry credentials and endpoints.
Advanced workflow patterns may require consulting Microsoft examples.

use_cases.title: Start an Enterprise Agent
use_cases.description: Create a Python Agent Framework project with Foundry model settings, server mode, and setup notes.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multi-Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Build workflow patterns that connect agents, executors, streaming events, and typed message edges.

use_cases.title: Prepare Local Debugging
use_cases.description: Generate VS Code debug tasks and launch settings for Agent Inspector based testing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one Python agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Python Microsoft Agent Framework agent that uses my Foundry project endpoint and deployment name. Include requirements and a README.

prompt_templates.title: Add Server Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my existing Agent Framework project to run as an HTTP server by default. Preserve CLI mode only if it already exists.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-agent workflow with writer and reviewer agents. Use streaming events and explain how each executor passes messages.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Debug Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate VS Code debug configuration for my Agent Framework server. Use localhost ports and explain what I must review before running it.

output_examples.input: Create a single Foundry-backed agent with server mode.
output: A Python project outline with an agent entrypoint, package requirements, environment placeholders, and server-mode guidance.
A README section that explains setup, configuration, startup, and local testing steps.

output_examples.input: Add debugging support for an Agent Framework workflow.
output: VS Code task and launch guidance for running the workflow with debugpy and Agent Inspector.
A short checklist for confirming ports, entrypoint names, and virtual environment paths before execution.

output_examples.output: A workflow design that names each agent, describes message flow, and explains expected streaming events.

best_practices: Confirm the Foundry endpoint and model deployment before writing environment configuration.
Review generated .env and .vscode files before running any debug task.
Pin package versions and update them only after compatibility testing.
anti_patterns: Do not store secrets directly in generated examples or shared documentation.
Do not run generated agents against production services before local review.
Do not rely on latest MCP packages without pinning or dependency review.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create Python Agent Framework agents, workflows, HTTP server entrypoints, and local debug configuration.

faq.question: Does it deploy agents?
faq.answer: No. It prepares project code and setup files, but deployment is outside this skill.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require Azure AI Foundry?
faq.answer: Most Foundry examples require a project endpoint, a model deployment name, and valid Azure credentials.

faq.question: What should I review before running output?
faq.answer: Review environment files, package versions, generated shell tasks, ports, and any MCP tool commands.

faq.question: Is it only for Python?
faq.answer: Yes. The included instructions and references target the Python Microsoft Agent Framework SDK.
